# X3P fixtures

`csafe-logo.x3p` is the existing real-world fixture. Its archive contains no
`ValidPointsLink` or validity member.

`validity-{i,l,f,d}.x3p` are tiny synthetic fixtures generated by
`python3 tests/fixtures/generate_validity_fixtures.py`. The same bytes are copied
to the R package's `inst/extdata` so installed-package tests exercise the same
files as Rust and Python.

Each fixture has a non-square 5-by-2 grid, X-fastest storage, and a packed
validity mask `95 fd` in hexadecimal. Bits are least-significant first and 1
means valid. The ten meaningful bits are
`1 0 1 0 1 0 0 1 1 0`. Unused final-byte bits are intentionally 1 and are ignored.
Integer I stores -10 through -1. Integer L stores 100000 through 100009.
Both have Z increment 0.5 and offset 100. Float F and D store 0 through 9 with
NaN at index 2, whose set validity bit cannot make its height usable.

The format decisions were checked against the primary
[openGPS X3P documentation](https://sourceforge.net/p/open-gps/mwiki/X3p/)
and its [ValidBuffer reference implementation, revision 402](https://svn.code.sf.net/p/open-gps/code/!svn/bc/402/ISO5436_XML/branches/Kohler_LinuxPort/src/ISO5436_2_XML/cxx/valid_buffer.cxx).
`ValidBuffer::IsValid` uses byte `index / 8` and bit `index % 8` with a left shift
from 1. `Allocate` rounds the byte count up and `AllocateRaw` initializes bytes
to 255, establishing that high padding bits may be set. The
[DataLink schema](https://svn.code.sf.net/p/open-gps/code/!svn/bc/402/ISO5436_XML/branches/Kohler_LinuxPort/src/ISO5436_2_XML/iso5436_2.xsd)
pairs `ValidPointsLink` with `MD5ChecksumValidPoints`. These fixtures were
written for Verity and contain no copied upstream scan data or source code.
